summary: Backend-only testing of the unencrypted full-snapshot change in /app/backend/recovery.py (and the daily scheduler helper in /app/backend/backups.py). 7/7 pytest tests PASS (100%). Verified: POST /api/admin/backups/full-snapshot returns 200 with encrypted=false, selfcheck_ok=true, passphrase_uploaded=false, filename ending in 'FULL SNAPSHOT.zip', selfcheck.has_code=true, and a real size_bytes>0. Drive is currently disconnected: gdrive_uploaded=false with gdrive_error in {'auth_expired','not_connected'} — expected per E1. Confirmed PLAIN-zip behavior independently via POST /api/admin/backups/verify with a freshly constructed plain ZIP + NO passphrase → 200 with valid=true, encrypted=false. Auth gating works: 401 with no Authorization header, 403 with non-admin token. Regression: GET /api/admin/backup-health (admin) → 200, GET /api/admin/gdrive/status (admin) → 200.
critical_code_review_comments: recovery.py still imports `pyzipper`, `secrets`, `string`, and keeps `_PASSPHRASE_ALPHABET` + `generate_passphrase()` + `passphrase_filename()` helpers. They are now dead code in the snapshot-creation path (still used by restore for legacy encrypted backups via _parse_backup_bytes / _zip_is_encrypted, which is correct). Consider a comment block noting these are restore-only helpers retained for backward compatibility — otherwise a future reader may try to remove them and break legacy restore.

RESTORE.md in the produced ZIP still references the 'PASSPHRASE' file in its conditional branch — the 'encrypt=False' branch is correctly used now, so the user-facing instructions are accurate. Just confirming the conditional logic in _build_full_snapshot is sound.

backups.py: docstring on _scheduler_loop still says 'Builds the FULL ENCRYPTED snapshot' but the implementation now calls _build_full_snapshot(..., encrypt=False). Update the docstring to avoid future confusion.

backups.py _alert_email_content body still mentions 'nightly encrypted backups' even though the offsite snapshot is now plaintext. Minor wording fix recommended so the admin alert email matches reality.
seed_data_creation: One transient non-admin user (testuser_<uuid>@example.com / Test12345!) per run for 403 gating. No persistent seed data added.
context_for_next_testing_agent: test_full_snapshot_plain.py is reusable. Uses EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL from frontend/.env and admin creds from /app/memory/test_credentials.md. The /api/admin/backups/full-snapshot call takes ~30-45s on this container (tar-gzips frontend+backend trees). The verify-with-plain-zip test builds a minimal in-memory ZIP {db.json + manifest.json} and asserts encrypted=false — this is a direct proof that the parser accepts plain ZIPs without a passphrase, independent of the snapshot endpoint. Drive is currently disconnected so gdrive_uploaded=false is expected.
rca_of_issue: N/A — validation of feature change. The plain-ZIP behavior is confirmed at three layers: (1) the snapshot endpoint reports encrypted=false + selfcheck_ok=true (selfcheck calls _parse_backup_bytes with passphrase=None on the freshly built archive and succeeds), (2) the /verify endpoint accepts a hand-rolled plain ZIP with no passphrase and reports encrypted=false, (3) passphrase_uploaded=false confirms no companion .txt is generated or pushed to Drive.
